oh_kiedaisch_point.blurb: A small sandstone crag on a wooded hillside above the Ohio River in Monroe County, close to the Hannibal bridge into West Virginia. Trad and sport routes are about evenly split, spread over several short walls. The grades run from easy fives into the low 5.12s, with 5.10 the biggest group and a solid supply of 5.7 to 5.9 climbs. It sees few regular visitors, so you can usually spread out, though road and river traffic carry up the slope. The hillside is shaded, so the rock may stay damp after rain.
oh_kiedaisch_point.parking_note: Pull off along either side of State Route 7, a bit over a mile north of the bridge at Hannibal. The trailhead sits beside a gravel driveway that heads up a small hollow.
oh_kiedaisch_point.approach: A signed trail climbs the hillside from the road for roughly a quarter to half a mile. Near the cliff it forks; the right branch runs along the base of the rock.

ok_slab_lands.blurb: A granite boulder field in the Dog Run Hollow section of the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge, set on a ridge with open prairie views. The problems range from big, proud boulders to smaller, friendlier ones, and the grades lean toward the easy and middle range, mostly V0 to V4, with a few harder lines up to V8. There is no maintained trail in, so expect to route-find across grass and rock. Bring pads and plenty of water, since shade is scarce, and treat the refuge with care; climbing here depends on visitors behaving well.
ok_slab_lands.parking_note: Leave the car at the Steak Dinner boulder pullout and stay within the designated parking spots.
ok_slab_lands.approach: From the parking spot, head east up the hill, cross the top, then follow the ridgeline to the big boulders. Only faint animal and boulderer paths exist.

ok_main_area.blurb: The core of Shotgun, a modest sandstone bouldering spot in the hills near Sand Springs, west of Tulsa. Problems are short, on scattered blocks such as a cube, a fridge-shaped boulder and a slab, with grades running from V0 through the middle range and a few hard lines in the double digits. The best of it is a handful of solid problems rather than a big circuit. Sandstone in this part of the state is soft and slow to dry, so give it several days after rain, and be considerate of neighbors and farm traffic when you park.

ok_pear_and_apple.blurb: A boulder field at the foot of the Pear and Apple, two enormous fruit-shaped granite domes in Charon's Garden Wilderness in the Wichita Mountains. Nearly all of the problems are bouldering, in clusters such as the Jungle Boulders, with grades from V0 up to V10 and a good number in the V3 to V6 range; a few trad, sport and top-rope lines are mixed in. It is a hike in a wild, rugged setting, with little shade and rough footing, so carry water, pads and a map. There are no fixed anchors and the ethic is to leave no trace.
ok_pear_and_apple.parking_note: Start from the Sunset picnic area lot on the refuge road and walk the main Charon's Garden trail.
ok_pear_and_apple.approach: Follow the Charon's Garden trail from the lot. After the first creek crossing, veer left and continue to a large A-shaped boulder, where the boulder field begins.

on_old_country.blurb: One of the largest and most climbed sectors of Niagara Glen, a wooded gorge reserve above the Niagara River just below the falls. Boulders sit among forest and talus along wooded trails, with problems from head height to a few meters tall. Grades run from V0 to V9, with the heart of the range around V3 and V4. It is a quiet escape from the tourist crowds, but weekends can fill the parking, so arrive early. Stay on marked trails to protect the plants.
on_old_country.parking_note: Use the Nature Centre lot on the Niagara Parkway, then walk to the large metal staircase that drops into the gorge.

on_romper_room.blurb: A busy bouldering sector of Niagara Glen, the wooded gorge reserve near the Niagara Whirlpool. Boulders are scattered through forest, with problems of moderate height. The grades are broad: a good selection of V0 to V3 for warm-ups, a deep middle in V4 to V6, and a few lines up past V9 into V10 and beyond. The reserve is protected habitat, so stay on the marked trails, keep groups small, and carry out everything you bring.
on_romper_room.parking_note: Use the Nature Centre lot on the Niagara Parkway, then walk to the large metal staircase that drops into the gorge.

on_land_of_oz.blurb: A sector of Niagara Glen, the forested gorge reserve beside the Niagara River, known for its playfully named areas. Land of Oz leans toward the approachable: roughly a third of the problems are V0 or V1, with plenty through V4 and a handful of harder lines up to V8. Boulders sit among trees on wooded trails, so expect uneven landings and bring ample pads. Sticking to marked paths helps protect the reserve's fragile plants.
on_land_of_oz.parking_note: Use the Nature Centre lot on the Niagara Parkway, then walk to the large metal staircase that drops into the gorge.

_expect.name: Rattle Snake Point West Cliff (aka Climbers LEFT of Steel Stairs

on_rattle_snake_point_west_cliff_aka_cli.blurb: The stretch of the West Cliff at Rattlesnake Point, on the Niagara Escarpment near Milton, that lies to the left of the steel stairs when you face out. Trad climbing dominates, with a good amount of bolted sport too. Most routes fall between 5.6 and 5.10, with a few easier warm-ups and some harder lines into 5.11, making it a good fit for moderate leaders. It is busy on weekends and gets a mix of sun and shade through the day. Use the existing anchors rather than trees.
on_rattle_snake_point_west_cliff_aka_cli.parking_note: Drive to the upper lot inside the park gate and follow the signed trail straight to the lookout stairs.
on_rattle_snake_point_west_cliff_aka_cli.approach: From the upper lot, walk the trail to the steel stairs and descend them; the first route starts right at the bottom, with the left-side climbs running along the base.
